questions.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(2t+7)\underset{\sim}{i}+(9-3t)\underset{\sim}{j}$.
What is its position when $t=5$?

options.why: Computed $3t-9=6$ instead of $9-3t=-6$, subtracting the wrong way round.
Added $t$ to $7$ instead of $2t$, giving $5+7=12$.
Added $t$ instead of $2t$ and also subtracted the wrong way round in the $\underset{\sim}{j}$ component.

questions.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{2}-5t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(3t+2)\underset{\sim}{j}$.
What is its position when $t=6$?

options.why: Read the second component as $2t+3$, giving $12+3=15$.
Read the first component as $(t-5)^{2}$, giving $1^{2}=1$.
Read the first component as $(t-5)^{2}$ and the second as $2t+3$.

questions.question_text:
A particle is at $(-4,6)$ when $t=0$.
Its $x$-coordinate increases by $5$ each second and its $y$-coordinate decreases by $2$ each second.
Which is its position vector function?

options.why: Added $2t$ although the $y$-coordinate is decreasing.
Swapped the starting value and the rate in the $\underset{\sim}{i}$ component.
Swapped starting value and rate in the $\underset{\sim}{i}$ component and added instead of subtracting in the $\underset{\sim}{j}$ component.

questions.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=6t\underset{\sim}{i}+(3t-1)\underset{\sim}{j}$.
How far is the particle from the origin when $t=2$?

options.why: Added the two components $12+5$ instead of using Pythagoras.
Subtracted the two components $12-5$ instead of using Pythagoras.
Found $12^{2}+5^{2}$ but did not take the square root.

questions.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{2}-16)\underset{\sim}{i}+(3t-5)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge0$.
At what time is the particle on the $y$-axis?

options.why: Took the negative square root, which is outside the given restriction $t\ge0$.
Solved $t^{2}=16$ as $t=16$ without taking a square root.
Set the $y$-component to zero, which is the condition for being on the $x$-axis.

questions.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=7\underset{\sim}{i}+(3-4t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge0$.
Which statement describes its motion?

options.text: It moves straight down the line $x=7$, starting at $(7,3)$.
It moves straight up the line $x=7$, starting at $(7,3)$.
options.why: Treated $3-4t$ as increasing, when the coefficient of $t$ is negative.

options.text: It moves straight left along the line $y=7$, starting at $(3,7)$.
options.why: Swapped the $\underset{\sim}{i}$ and $\underset{\sim}{j}$ components, so the fixed value was read as the $y$-coordinate.

options.text: It moves straight right along the line $y=7$, starting at $(3,7)$.
options.why: Swapped the components and also treated $3-4t$ as increasing.

questions.solution_text:
$x(t)=7$ for every value of $t$, so the particle stays on the line $x=7$.
$y(t)=3-4t$ decreases by $4$ each second, starting at $y=3$.
The particle moves straight down the line $x=7$, starting at $(7,3)$.

questions.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=8\cos t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+8\sin t\,\underset{\sim}{j}$.
What is its exact position when $t=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$?

options.why: Swapped the values of $\cos\frac{\pi}{3}$ and $\sin\frac{\pi}{3}$.
Used $\sin\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{1}{2}$ instead of $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.
Used $\cos\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ instead of $\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.question_text:
A particle moves in a straight line at a steady rate.
It is at $(3,10)$ when $t=1$ and at $(19,-2)$ when $t=5$.
Which is its position vector function?

options.why: Used $+3$ per second although the $y$-coordinate fell from $10$ to $-2$.
Used the position at $t=1$ as the position at $t=0$ instead of tracking back one second.
Used the position at $t=1$ as the position at $t=0$ and took the $y$-rate as $+3$.

questions.solution_text:
Change in position over $4$ seconds $=(19-3)\underset{\sim}{i}+(-2-10)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=16\underset{\sim}{i}-12\underset{\sim}{j}$
Change each second $=4\underset{\sim}{i}-3\underset{\sim}{j}$
Position at $t=0$ $=(3-4)\underset{\sim}{i}+(10+3)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=-\underset{\sim}{i}+13\underset{\sim}{j}$
$\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(4t-1)\underset{\sim}{i}+(13-3t)\underset{\sim}{j}$
